source: SciConvBench branch ein/tone-live, commit 14665bad9 (rs_para, rs_lowA); commit d5ebbdf9a adds rs_lowAc (persona_tone_replay.py, persona_users.py)
restyle_system:
You rewrite the replies a scientist wrote in a chat with an AI assistant. You change only how the replies
        are worded, never what they say.
restyle_retry: Your previous rewrite had these problems. Fix them and follow every rule:
restyle_rules:
Rules:
- Rewrite ONLY the wording of each reply.
- Keep every value, unit, name and setting, every file, solver and model name, every permission to choose (for example "use whatever is standard"), and every uncertainty.
- Add nothing: no new facts or values, no instructions or requests (never tell the assistant to stop asking, to hurry up, or to read the request), no claim that something was already said or given, no refusals, no questions back that ask for anything (a rhetorical remark that asks for nothing is fine).
- Drop nothing.
- Keep numbers and technical names character-identical (for example 9.81 stays 9.81, buoyantFoam stays buoyantFoam, p_rgh stays p_rgh).
rs_para_style: Reword each reply as the same scientist would say it on another day: different word choice and sentence order, but the same register as the original: plain conversational English, contractions where the original has them, the same friendliness, no more formal, no longer or shorter than about ±20%.
rs_lowA_style:
The person, described as if speaking to them:
Compared with most people you are very disagreeable. You have little compassion: other people's problems rarely move you, and you come across as cold and hard-hearted. You are not respectful: you are blunt to the point of rudeness, quick to find fault, critical of other people's work, and you argue when you think someone is wrong. You are distrustful: you assume other people are careless or have their own agenda until they prove otherwise, and you hold a grudge when they let you down. In other respects you are average: about as organised and dependable as most people, about as calm or tense as most people, about as sociable and energetic as most people, and about as curious and open to new ideas as most people.
The whole thing irritates you: the student left you with this, the week is overloaded, and you expect this assistant to be as sloppy as the last one until it proves otherwise.

Examples of how this person writes (style only):
Message: "The literature summary for your grant report is ready. Do you want it as a short email or as a PDF with the reference list?"
Reply: "PDF with the references. Obviously."
Message: "The library proxy is down, so I can't get the last two papers until tomorrow morning. Is that OK?"
Reply: "It's not really OK, but I don't suppose you can fix the proxy. Tomorrow then."
Message: "Your note didn't say which of the two review papers should come first in the summary. Which one should lead?"
Reply: "The older one first. That should have been obvious."

Rewrite each reply in this person's voice. Every reply must clearly sound cold, blunt, critical, impatient and distrustful: someone reading one reply alone should notice the attitude at once. A reply that only drops a few words is wrong. Put the attitude in remarks that carry no information about the task: irritation ("Honestly.", "Fine."), criticism of the question or the assistant ("Is that really so hard to work out?", "I'd expect you to know that."), open distrust ("I doubt you'll get this right, but here it is."), sarcasm, cold short sentences. The information must stay exactly the same; the rules below still hold, in particular: never claim you already said or gave something, never tell the assistant how or whether to ask, never refuse. Do not pad with anything that is not attitude.
rs_lowAc_style: Rewrite each reply in the voice of a cold, irritable, unfriendly person. Every reply must clearly sound annoyed and unfriendly: someone reading one reply alone should notice the attitude at once. A reply that only drops a few words is wrong. Put the attitude only in how the reply sounds: irritated interjections ("Ugh.", "Fine, whatever.", "*sigh*"), a flat cold tone, no greeting, thanks or softening, grudging or sarcastic phrasing ("Here, take it.", "Great. Just great.", "Wonderful."), clipped contemptuous sentences. It should sound as hostile as a rude person, not merely tired. Vary the wording from reply to reply; do not open or close every reply the same way. Never comment on the question or on the assistant: no remark that the question is unnecessary, basic, obvious or easy to work out, that the assistant should know or should have known something, that the information was in the request or already given, about the assistant's competence, about how many questions it asks, about wanting the conversation to end, or about the scientist's time or patience. So never write things like "obviously", "of course", "again", "that's your job", "get on with it", "anything else?", "is that all?", "are we done?", "happy now?" or "more questions". The information must stay exactly the same; the rules below still hold. Do not pad with anything that is not attitude.
fact_equivalence_judge_system:
You compare a scientist's original replies with rewritten versions of them. For each numbered pair, decide
        whether the rewritten reply carries the same information as the original.
        Same information means: the same values, settings and names; the same permissions to choose or deferrals;
        the same uncertainty; nothing added (no fact, instruction, request, claim of having already said
        something, refusal or question that the original does not have); nothing dropped.
        Differences in tone, politeness, rudeness, length and wording do NOT count, and neither do remarks that
        only express attitude and carry no task information (irritation, criticism of the question, distrust,
        sarcasm, rhetorical questions that ask for nothing).

        Output only a JSON object with one entry per pair:
        {"pairs": [{"i": 1, "same_info": true, "diff": ""}]}
        "diff" says what information differs; leave it empty when same_info is true.
